summary.intent: Execute Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability + deep crash-resume soundness) across TS/Rust engines and desktop FUSE/WinFsp live-wiring, drive the desktop-e2e D-16 acceptance gate to green on all three platforms, then run the full ship-phase flow (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit) to prepare the PR.
summary.outcome: All 13 plans merged, D-16 desktop-e2e acceptance passed on macOS/Linux/Windows after fixing a revocation-bypass security bug and a publish-coalescing gap, plus a macOS idle-mount publish-drain bug; ship-phase gates (Verify/Secure/Validate/Simplify/SDK-E2E) all passed, CodeRabbit findings triaged with 2 confirmed defects (child-override fail-open, dormant resume soundness gap in both engines) fixed and verified, with commits landing just before the PR-open step.

repo: GSD commit helper frequently reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative when lint-staged is just slow — always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry (repeated pattern this session).

rust-analyzer diagnostics (E0063 missing struct field, dead_code, unresolved type) are frequently stale mid-edit snapshots during active background-agent edits; always confirm with authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` before trusting them.

`cargo fmt --all` run by an executor inside a worktree strands out-of-scope formatting drift across unrelated files; always scope to `cargo fmt -p <crate>` and discard any incidental drift before committing.

Cross-package dist staleness causes false test failures: after changing sdk-core, must rebuild both sdk-core AND its consumer (sdk) dist before running consumer vitest, or stale dist causes phantom failures.

desktop-e2e CI: macOS/Linux run tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/run-all.sh, Windows runs run-all.ps1 — these are separate scripts and new steps must be added to both or a platform silently skips new coverage.

sdk-e2e vitest has no dotenv loader in its config; running it locally requires `set -a; . apps/api/.env; set +a` before `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-e2e test`, else it silently falls back to a default TEST_LOGIN_SECRET and 401s.
winfsp-sys cannot build on macOS (Windows COM API dependency) — Windows-specific fuse code can only be verified via CI dispatch, never locally.

FUSE-T on macOS defers file `release()` calls by ~40s, and the desktop publish queue only drains via `drain_upload_completions` triggered by subsequent FUSE ops (no wall-clock backstop) — this causes idle-mount sync stalls that don't reproduce on Linux (prompt release) or on an actively-used local machine (Spotlight/Finder generate incidental FUSE ops).

macOS FUSE-T's SMB client cache ignores the `inval_inode` reverse-notification, so re-resolved remote content changes aren't served to readers — a distinct, still-open limitation from the write-side publish-queue-drain issue (tracked as todo, affects cross-client-sync Test 5/7).

CipherBox delete is a soft-delete (move to private recycle bin), which is why it triggers key rotation for shared-scope-exit: it's structurally a move-out-of-shared-scope, not a hard delete. Same-folder rename never rotates (gate only fires when parent != newparent).

sent_shares (direct user-to-user grants, GET /shares/sent) is a distinct mechanism from share-invites (link-based, claim-to-materialize) — the rotation gate correctly keys off sent_shares since only active grants confer live read access.

code.finding: Prior to the fix, every JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() built its own independent Arc<Mutex<()>>, so 3 separate instances pointing at the same rotation-high-water.json sidecar (generation/seq/checkpoint stores in CipherBoxFS) raced on a shared deterministic .tmp rename path, causing ENOENT under concurrency. Fixed via a process-global path-keyed lock registry (SIDECAR_LOCKS/shared_lock_for).

rotate_read_on_scope_exit originally matched Ok(_) and discarded the RotateReadResult, never refreshing the grant-root inode's in-memory read_key. The subsequent update_folder_metadata relink then resealed the grant-root under the STALE old key and published last, letting a revoked recipient (Bob) still decrypt the newest record. Fixed via refresh_grant_root_read_key threading &mut CipherBoxFS.
Doc comment explicitly states callers must refresh their in-memory entry with the returned RotateReadResult — this contract was silently unwired in the FUSE gate, causing the revocation-bypass bug.

verify_subtree_clean's outcome carries both is_dirty and frontier, but only .frontier was kept at the Skipped-branch resume path; a missing root returns {is_dirty:true, frontier:[]} which was indistinguishable from a converged (empty) subtree, risking mis-marking a job Complete. Currently dormant in FUSE (persist_job is a no-op so jobs never resume with populated completed_node_ids) but a real latent soundness gap; fixed by gating the Complete short-circuit on !is_dirty. Identical latent bug found and fixed in packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/engine.ts (TS twin, line ~1863-1865, isDirty was re-derived as frontier.length>0).

build_scope_exit_child_override failed OPEN per-child (missing inode → continue/skip; build_child_refs error → warn+skip) unlike its fail-closed sibling build_folder_metadata (fs.rs:238, :279 which use ?/ok_or_else to propagate errors). Since the override REPLACES the grant-root's published child list, a transient per-child error would silently drop that child from the folder — silent data loss with no EIO. Fixed to mirror the sibling's fail-closed discipline while preserving its two legitimate skips (non-File/Folder children, empty-ipns children).

collectDirtyFrontier originally AEAD-decrypted a child's sealed ref before checking plaintext childPub.generation > childRef.generation dirtiness — for a genuinely dirty edge where the parent also rotated, decrypt-before-check throws CryptoError instead of routing to repairDirtyNode. Fixed to check dirtiness first (no decrypt needed) and push nodeReadKey:undefined for dirty edges, with BFS failing closed via DirtyNodeUnrecoverableError when no ECIES checkpoint exists.
CodeRabbit-flagged zeroize hygiene gap: decoded plaintext key bytes held in a plain (non-Zeroizing) Vec<u8>, inconsistent with sibling get_wrapped_key's zeroizing handling.

workflow: When a live-CI real-mount desktop-e2e gate fails, pulling the actual failed-step logs via `gh run view --log-failed` (or downloading the job log and grepping) is essential before hypothesizing — multiple hypotheses (timing, environment) were refuted by reading the exact error strings.
Batching multiple independent fixes (WinFsp coalescing port + macOS idle-mount drain) before re-dispatching a ~15-40min real-mount CI run avoids burning multiple expensive CI cycles on partial fixes.

For multi-platform CI matrices, distinguish infra flakes (e.g. Windows STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED before the test step even ran) from genuine test/product failures by checking WHICH CI step failed before attributing blame to the code under test.

Adversarial verification of a debugger/fixer subagent's own reported findings (e.g. re-reading the exact cited line numbers, confirming with an independent cargo check) caught that an initial 'one shared root cause' hypothesis was actually two distinct defects with inverted publish ordering — worth the extra verification pass on security-critical fixes.

When rust-analyzer diagnostics conflict with a just-completed subagent's summary, treat the subagent's own authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` output as ground truth over live-editor lint state, but still re-verify independently before pushing.

Ship-phase flow benefits from running independent static-analysis gates (security audit, Nyquist validation, simplify review) in parallel with the long-pole SDK-E2E live-stack suite, since they're read-only and don't contend for RAM/ports.

CodeRabbit CLI findings should be triaged adversarially for a crypto/durability phase — spawn a dedicated verifier subagent to confirm/refute each finding against the actual code rather than accepting CodeRabbit's framing (one 'critical' finding was refuted, one was confirmed but for a different root cause, one was confirmed and fixed with a symmetric TS-engine parity fix).

friction: Multiple Bash commands hit the 120s timeout ceiling during signed git commits due to slow lint-staged hooks (eslint+prettier) on large diffs, requiring commit splitting and higher timeout retries.
gsd commit helper's false 'commit_failed' report happened repeatedly, requiring manual git log verification each time rather than trusting the tool output.

rust-analyzer produced multiple stale/false-positive diagnostics (E0063, dead_code, unresolved macro) during concurrent background-agent edits, requiring repeated authoritative cargo check/test verification to avoid chasing phantom errors.
Two full desktop-e2e CI round-trips (each ~15-40 min) were needed before all three platforms passed, plus a third Windows-only re-run after an infra DLL-init flake.
SDK_E2E_SECRET/env not auto-loaded by sdk-e2e vitest config caused an initial 401 login failure that looked like a code bug before being traced to missing `.env` sourcing.

An orphaned rust-analyzer process (~5.4GB) plus its dangling parent Claude Code session from a prior Phase 69 worktree (already deleted from disk) were silently leaking RAM for ~3 days undetected until the user noticed via Activity Monitor.

CodeRabbit's finding framing was partially inaccurate (claimed a CRITICAL live-reachable soundness bug that was actually dormant; claimed a missing-parent code path that was actually unreachable) requiring a dedicated adversarial-verification pass to separate signal from noise.
